scope.surface: Settings navigation state plus Beta and Archive light-theme content

productLoss: Lynx gives the Providers navigation row a selected background on every Settings route through .settings-nav__item--providers, even when another route is active.

The Lynx navigation host also promotes the Providers icon and label through isActive || item.to === /settings/providers, so Beta and Archive each show two visual selections while Web shows exactly one.
Beta and Archive content are otherwise close to the current Web authority; the highest localized new loss is the false navigation state rather than the page body.
harnessMismatch: The first Beta light capture failed only because the light-theme gate required the chat Sidebar footer. Settings uses its own settings-nav footer and Back action; the harness now measures and gates that real anatomy.

Earlier navigation diagnostics recorded only semantic active classes and missed CSS-only selection. The current hard gate records both semantic active and computed visual selection, and intentionally rejects the false Providers highlight.
intentionalPlatformDelta: The Lynx Settings rail uses 44px touch rows and a 60px footer while Web uses denser 32px rows and a 48px footer. This touch-density difference remains explicit and is not attributed to the false-selection fix.
acceptedRenderingNoise: Fractional text and row-height differences below one pixel are retained as rendering noise where content and outer allocation match.
classification.evidenceBoundary: Both baselines use one immutable loopback snapshot, the same light theme, 1280x820 panes, shipping Web and Lynx-for-Web bundles, canonical routes, matching content identity, clean consoles, and zero agent-browser leaks. The hard-gated samples intentionally fail only finalSettingsNavigationReady and are retained as the product-loss baseline.

validation.hardGate: Both current products fail only finalSettingsNavigationReady.
